Monoclonal antisera are derived from a single B cell clone, producing antibodies targeting one epitope of an antigen. Polyclonal antisera come from multiple B cell clones, producing antibodies against multiple epitopes of an antigen.  
Option (A) is incorrect because monoclonal antibodies target one region of one antigen, but polyclonal antibodies target multiple regions of the *same* antigen (not different antigens).  
Option (B) is incorrect because monoclonal antibodies do not react with multiple regions of an antigen.  
Option (C) correctly states the cellular origin and specificity: monoclonal from a single B lymphocyte’s descendants, polyclonal from different B lymphocytes’ descendants.  
Option (D) is incorrect because polyclonal antisera come from B lymphocytes, not T lymphocytes (T cells do not secrete antibodies).  

Final answer: (C)
